#!/bin/bash
#flux: --job-name=priorgrad
#flux: --nodes=1
#flux: --gpus-per-node=1
#flux: --output=priorgrad.o%J
#flux: --mail-user=s2212015@jaist.ac.jp
#flux: --mail-type=BEGIN,END
# The PBS queue directive '-q GPU-1' does not have a direct equivalent in Flux.
# This is typically handled by resource constraints. You may need to add a
# '--constraint' option if the target system uses node features.
# The PBS directive '-j oe' to join stdout and stderr was translated by setting only the
# --output directive, which will capture both streams by default in this configuration.
# The PBS mail trigger '-m be' (begin, end) was translated to '--mail-type=BEGIN,END'.

module load singularity

# The 'cd' command is preserved as it changes to a user's home directory subdirectory, not the job submission directory.
cd ~/HifiDiff

# Note: The output from the python command is being redirected to 'logs/priorgrad.log'.
# The job's main output file (specified by #flux: --output) will only contain output
# from commands outside of the singularity execution, if any.
singularity exec -i --nv ~/pytorch_22.02-py3.sif python __main__.py \
    configs/priorgrad.py \
    checkpoints/priorgrad \
    /home/s2212015/LJSpeech-1.1 \
    filelists/train.txt \
    --max_steps 1000000 --validate_loop 10000 --save_ckpt_loop 50000 >> logs/priorgrad.log 2>&1

issues: The script's output handling can be confusing. It uses a Flux directive (`--output`) to set a job-level output file (`priorgrad.o%J`), but then the main application command redirects both its stdout and stderr to a different file (`>> logs/priorgrad.log 2>&1`). This means the scheduler's log file will be mostly empty, and all important application output will be in `logs/priorgrad.log`. This can make debugging difficult if the script fails before the `singularity exec` command is reached.
